description_full: The RealReal, Inc. operates an online marketplace for resale luxury goods worldwide. It provides a range of product categories, including women's fashion, men's fashion, jewelry, and watches. The company sells products through its website, online marketplace, mobile app, and retail stores. The RealReal, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
ceo_bio: Ms. Rati Sahi Levesque | President, CEO & Director | Age 44 | Compensation: $2.1M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 3K people. Revenue per employee of $221K ranks in the bottom quartile among Consumer Cyclical peers, with revenue growing 14%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $6K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $9K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 10× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (8/10).
financial_summary: The RealReal, Inc. is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $1.4B market cap on $693M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +4.6pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Gross margins of 64% are the starting point for assessing pricing power.
The business throws off $18M in free cash flow — roughly 3 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin -0.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 6.9% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
